title: Propagate the merit-over-cost rule to subagent-planner (both copies)
description:
CAM-379 propagated the operator's merit-over-cost recommendation rule to the three cam agents that BUILD, GATE, and APPROVE (subagent-implementer, subagent-reviewer, subagent-auditor) in both .claude/agents/ and templates/agents/. The subagent-planner was left out and genuinely lacks the rule in both copies (verified: exhaustive grep for merit/over-cost/operational-cost/context-window/effort/undersize/oversize/scope-limiter returns only the frontmatter 'effort: xhigh'; the planner body never mentions cost, effort, 'v1', or 'future enhancement'). This is the last hole in the think->build->gate->approve governance chain: the planner AUTHORS the PRD scope and story decomposition, so it is precisely the agent that could undersize, oversize, or weaken a story's design approach for effort or cost reasons.

Scope: add a 'Merit over cost.' rule to the planner's '## Story Sizing Rules' section in BOTH .claude/agents/subagent-planner.md and templates/agents/subagent-planner.md, with planner-role framing (do not undersize/oversize/weaken a story's approach for cost reasons; rank by engineering merit; if a robust approach is expensive, note the cost separately after the recommendation without changing what is planned). The two must-survive clauses from CAM-379 must appear verbatim: (A) 'This rule limits the quality of the recommendation, not its scope: Simplicity remains the scope limiter.' and (B) 'Operational cost is never a criterion, but quality degradation from context-window exhaustion is a quality criterion, not a cost one.'

The two planner copies are currently byte-identical (205 lines, no deliberate divergence), so the inserted prose must be identical text in both. Because templates/agents/ is embedded into the compiled binary via scripts/generate-embedded-vendor.ts (src/vendor/_generated.ts), editing the templates copy requires an embed-vendor regen, and the change ships to adopters via a future cam init, so a coherence rebuild is required after merge.

Out of scope: do NOT change the implementer/reviewer/auditor/orchestrator copies (already done in CAM-379); do NOT reword the two must-survive clauses; do NOT reconcile the two planner copies into a shared file.

spec.scope:
Add a 'Merit over cost.' rule to the subagent-planner agent in BOTH copies (.claude/agents/subagent-planner.md and templates/agents/subagent-planner.md), closing the last gap in the think->build->gate->approve governance chain (CAM-379 already covered implementer/reviewer/auditor; the orchestrator already had it). Insert this EXACT bullet at the end of the '## Story Sizing Rules' section (after the last 'Too big -- split these' bullet, before the '## Story Ordering' heading), IDENTICALLY in both copies:

- **Merit over cost.** When you author a story's scope, design approach, or acceptance criteria, rank the options by engineering merit (quality, launch-readiness) and never undersize, oversize, or weaken a story's approach because a stronger one costs more effort or looks like "v1", "future enhancement", or added complexity. If the robust approach is expensive, note the cost as a separate factor after the recommendation -- it does not change what you plan. This rule limits the quality of the recommendation, not its scope: Simplicity remains the scope limiter. Operational cost is never a criterion, but quality degradation from context-window exhaustion is a quality criterion, not a cost one.

After editing the templates copy, regenerate the embedded vendor blob (bun run embed-vendor) so src/vendor/_generated.ts is refreshed and embed-vendor:check passes. Surgical to the planner only.

The .claude planner copy carries the dictated planner-role framing phrase. [oracle: grep -q 'undersize, oversize, or weaken' .claude/agents/subagent-planner.md]
The templates planner copy carries the dictated planner-role framing phrase. [oracle: grep -q 'undersize, oversize, or weaken' templates/agents/subagent-planner.md]

The inserted planner rule preserves both must-survive clauses verbatim, uses planner-role framing about authoring and sizing story scope (not building/gating/approving), sits in the '## Story Sizing Rules' section, is consistent with the CAM-379 framing shipped in implementer/reviewer/auditor, and both planner copies remain byte-identical. [oracle: reviewer-judgment]
gotchas: The two planner copies (.claude/agents/subagent-planner.md and templates/agents/subagent-planner.md) are currently byte-identical (205 lines) with NO deliberate divergence: insert IDENTICAL text at the same location in both; do NOT reconcile them into a shared file and do NOT introduce divergence.
The two must-survive clauses (scope-limiter and context-window) must be copied VERBATIM from the reviewer/implementer/auditor version shipped in CAM-379; do not reword or paraphrase them.

Insert into the '## Story Sizing Rules' section, after the last 'Too big -- split these' bullet and before the '## Story Ordering' heading. That is the planner's sizing surface, the exact cost-temptation point.

templates/agents/ is embedded into the compiled binary via scripts/generate-embedded-vendor.ts (output src/vendor/_generated.ts). After editing the templates copy, run `bun run embed-vendor` or embed-vendor:check fails CI.

domainTerms: merit-over-cost rule: governance rule that recommendations are ranked by engineering merit (quality, launch-readiness) and never downgraded for execution cost/effort.
must-survive clauses: the two verbatim sentences (scope-limiter clause A and context-window clause B) that must appear identically across every cam agent copy.
embed-vendor: the regen step (bun scripts/generate-embedded-vendor.ts) that compiles templates/ into src/vendor/_generated.ts for the binary.
dual-copy: the .claude/agents/ (project) vs templates/agents/ (adopter-facing) copies of each agent instruction file.
